newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Van Ommeren, Pakhoed cooperate in China terminal.
newsitem.headline: Van Ommeren, Pakhoed cooperate in China terminal.

text.p: Shipping and tank storage firm Koninklijke van Ommeren NV and Pakhoed said on Thursday they will cooperate in tank storage activities in the port of Zhuhai in China.
Both Van Ommeren and Pakhoed will take a 47.5 percent stake in the VOPAK terminal.
Chinese partner Zhuhai International Engineering and Consulting Company will take the remaining five percent, they said in a statement.
Initial building for 175,000 cubic metre storage capacity will cost $85 million. The next phase will increase capacity to 320,000 cubic metres.
The terminal should be in operation in 1998.
"The cooperation between Van Ommeren and Pakhoed remains limited to the terminal in Zhuhai," they said.
Both companies said they had originally planned to build separate, but neighbouring, terminals in the harbour of Zhuhai.
"The location, the scale of investment and the possibilities for stronger growth were the reasons for our decision to cooperate," they said.
